tax.text: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, or EBITDA, a non-GAAP financial measure, represents net income (computed in accordance with GAAP) plus depreciation and amortization, interest expense, and income taxes. Same Store.text: We report in two segments, Same Store and Non-Same Store and Other. Our Same Store segment represents those apartment communities that have been owned and stabilized for at least 12 months as of the first day of the calendar year. Communities are considered stabilized when achieving 90% average physical occupancy for 90 days. Our Non-Same Store and Other segment includes recently acquired communities, communities being developed or in lease-up, communities that have been disposed of or identified for disposition, communities that have incurred a significant casualty loss and stabilized communities that do not meet the requirements to be Same Store communities. Also included in our Non-Same Store and Other segment are non-multifamily activities and expenses related to severe weather events, including hurricanes and winter storms. Additional information regarding the composition of our segments is included in Note 11 to the condensed consolidated financial statements included in this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q.

opex.text:
Property operating expenses include costs for property personnel, building repairs and maintenance, real estate taxes, insurance, utilities, landscaping and other operating expenses. The following table reflects our property operating expenses by segment for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 (dollars in thousands):

The increase in property operating expenses for our Same Store segment for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025 was primarily driven by increases in utilities expense of $2.0 million, building repair and maintenance expense of $1.4 million, and marketing expense of $1.0 million. The increase in property operating expenses from the Non-Same Store and Other segment for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025 was primarily the result of increased operating expenses from completed units in development communities and recently acquired communities.

nonop.heading: Other Income and Expenses
nonop.text:
Property management expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 were $18.2 million, consistent with the three months ended September 30, 2025. General and administrative expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 were $13.4 million, an increase of $0.9 million as compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025.

Interest expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $54.6 million, an increase of $8.3 million as compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily due to an increase in our average outstanding debt balance and an increase of 7 basis points in our effective interest rate during the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025.

Other non-operating (income) expense, net for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $3.0 million of income, an increase of $4.3 million as compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025. The income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was primarily driven by $2.4 million of income included in legal (recoveries), costs and settlements, net.

tax.text: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, or EBITDA, a non-GAAP financial measure, represents net income (computed in accordance with GAAP) plus depreciation and amortization, interest expense, and income taxes. As an owner and operator of real estate, management considers EBITDA to be an important measure of performance from core operations because EBITDA excludes various expense items that are not indicative of operating performance. EBITDA should not be considered as an alternative to net income, or any other GAAP measurement, as an indicator of operating performance or as an alternative to cash flow from operating, investing and financing activities as a measure of liquidity.

net.text: For the three months ended September 30, 2026, net income available for MAA common shareholders was $83.1 million as compared to $98.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Results for the three months ended September 30, 2026 included legal (recoveries), costs and settlements, net of $1.0 million, consisting of $2.4 million of income recorded in “Other non-operating (income) expense, net,” partially offset by $1.5 million of expense recorded in “(Expense) income from real estate joint venture.” Results for the three months ended September 30, 2025 included $8.9 million of accrued legal defense costs, partially offset by $5.4 million of non-cash gain from investments and $2.0 million of non-cash gain related to the fair value adjustment of the embedded derivative in the MAA Series I preferred stock. Revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased 1.0% as compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025. Property operating expenses, excluding depreciation and amortization, for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased by 2.9% as compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025. The primary drivers of these changes are discussed in the “Results of Operations” section.

ocf.heading: Cash Flows from Operating Activities
ocf.text: Net cash provided by operating activities was $739.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, a decrease of $76.9 million as compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease in operating cash flows was primarily driven by the timing of cash payments.

da.heading: Depreciation and Amortization
da.text: Depreciation and amortization expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $166.7 million, an increase of $10.1 million as compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was primarily driven by the recognition of depreciation expense associated with our completed development communities, acquisitions and capital spend activities completed after September 30, 2025 in the normal course of business through September 30, 2026.

capex.text: We expect that our primary uses of cash will be to fund our ongoing operating needs, to fund our ongoing capital spending requirements, which relate primarily to our development, redevelopment and property repositioning activities, to repay maturing borrowings, to fund the future acquisition of assets, to repurchase common shares and to pay shareholder dividends. We expect to meet our cash requirements through net cash flows from operating activities, existing unrestricted cash and cash equivalents, borrowings under our commercial paper program and our revolving credit facility, the future issuance of debt and equity and the future disposition of assets.

net sales.heading: Property Revenues
net sales.text:
The following table reflects our property revenues by segment for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 (dollars in thousands):

The Same Store segment generated a 0.4% decrease in revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2026, which is the result of average physical occupancy decrease of 0.3% and average effective rent per unit decrease of 0.1% as compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in property revenues from the Non-Same Store and Other segment for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025 was primarily the result of increased revenues from completed units in development communities and recently acquired communities.

Same Store.text: We report in two segments, Same Store and Non-Same Store and Other. Our Same Store segment represents those apartment communities that have been owned and stabilized for at least a full 12 months as of the first day of the calendar year. Communities are considered stabilized when achieving 90% average physical occupancy for 90 days. Our Non-Same Store and Other segment includes recently acquired communities, communities being developed or in lease-up, communities that have been disposed of or identified for disposition, communities that have experienced a significant casualty loss and stabilized communities that do not meet the requirements to be Same Store communities. Also included in our Non-Same Store and Other segment are non-multifamily activities and expenses related to severe weather events, including hurricanes and winter storms. Additional information regarding the composition of our segments is included in Note 11 to the condensed consolidated financial statements included in this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q.

Non Same Store And Other.text: We report in two segments, Same Store and Non-Same Store and Other. Our Same Store segment represents those apartment communities that have been owned and stabilized for at least a full 12 months as of the first day of the calendar year. Communities are considered stabilized when achieving 90% average physical occupancy for 90 days. Our Non-Same Store and Other segment includes recently acquired communities, communities being developed or in lease-up, communities that have been disposed of or identified for disposition, communities that have experienced a significant casualty loss and stabilized communities that do not meet the requirements to be Same Store communities. Also included in our Non-Same Store and Other segment are non-multifamily activities and expenses related to severe weather events, including hurricanes and winter storms. Additional information regarding the composition of our segments is included in Note 11 to the condensed consolidated financial statements included in this Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q.

Unless the context otherwise requires, all references to “MAA” refer only to Mid-America Apartment Communities, Inc., and not any of its consolidated subsidiaries.
